Author: Sujoy Paul
Bench: Sujoy Paul

In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Jabalpur Cra No. 196 of 2024 (Shiva Vs
The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others) Dated : 14-03-2024 Shri Sharad Verma-
Advocate for the appellant.

entities.text: High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri S.K. Kashyap - Government Advocate for the State.

Shri Shashank Upadhyay - Advocate for the
objector

Heard on I.A. No. 164 of 2024, application under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to appellant - Shiva arising out of judgment dated 21.12.2023 delivered in SC/79/2022 passed by Third Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (POCSO), Sagar, (M.P.).

entities.text: Third Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (POCSO), Sagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appellant has been convicted under Section 366 of the I.P.C. and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 5 years with fine of Rs.1,000/-, Section 6 POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 20 years with fine of Rs.5,000/- with default stipulation.

and for Section 376(2)(N) and Section 363 of the I.P.C.,
no separate sentence have been awarded.

Learned counsel for the appellant while pressing the application for suspension of sentence of the appellant submits that the prosecutrix in her statements recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. had clearly stated that she had gone with the present appellant out of her own will and she was in romantic relationship with the appellant.

It is further argued that the victim has supported the prosecution case in court statement but looking to the situation that she was willingly living with the appellant and worked in factory near Delhi for near about one month, it is a case of consent
On the aspect of determination of age, it is argued that there is overwriting of the name of mother in the scholar register Ex P/17-C.
It is argued that as per the scholar register, the age of the prosecutrix on the date of incident is 17 years 4 months and the determination of age is erroneous.
It is argued that the doctor PW/5 has opined that looking to the physical development of prosecutrix she was more than 18 years of age on the date of medical examination.

By referring to the statement of the prosecutrix, it is argued that looking to para 5 deposition of victim she must be more than 18 years of age on the date of incident and also that it has come in the statement of the prosecution witnesses that the victim was studying in College on the date of incident.
It is further submitted that the appellant is 21 years of age and the present appeal is of the years 2024.
Final hearing of this appeal is not possible in near future.
Thus, remaining jail sentence of the present appellant may be suspended.
Learned Government Counsel for the State as well as counsel for objector opposed the prayer for suspension of sentence.

Considering the aforesaid factual backdrop and without expressing any conclusive opinion on the Shiva vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147323117/
1 merits of the case, we deem it proper to suspend the remaining jail sentence of this appellant.

entities.text: Shiva vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, I.A. No. 164/2024 is allowed.

Subject to depositing the fine amount (if not already deposited), the remaining jail sentence of this appellant is hereby suspended and it is directed that the appellant - Shiva be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court with a further direction to appear before the trial Court, Sagar on 06.05.2024 and also on such further dates as may be fixed by the trial Court in this regard during the pendency of this appeal.
Certified copy as per rules.
